title: Coffee polyphenol consumption improves postprandial hyperglycemia associated with impaired vascular endothelial function in healthy male adults - ScienceDirect

Correlation analysis showed postprandial FMD was negatively associated with blood glucose increase after ingestion of the CPE beverage. In conclusion, these results suggest that coffee polyphenol consumption improves postprandial hyperglycemia and vascular endothelial function, which is associated with increased GLP-1 secretion and decreased oxidative stress in healthy humans.
Taking these previous findings together, we hypothesized that coffee polyphenol consumption may improve postprandial hyperglycemia and vascular endothelial function by stimulating postprandial GLP-1 release and/or reducing oxidative stress in healthy humans.
First, postprandial hyperglycemia was significantly decreased by the consumption of CPE in healthy male subjects, especially in those with lower insulinogenic index. Second, vascular endothelial function after meal ingestion was significantly improved by coffee polyphenol consumption.
In addition, Zhang and Zhang (2018) demonstrate in a meta-analysis study that coffee consumption was associated with a reduction in serum C-Reactive Protein (Zhang and Zhang, 2018). Also, a randomized, acute, crossover, intervention study with healthy male adults, found that coffee polyphenol consumption reduced the hyperglycemia and improved vascular endothelial function in healthy humans (Jokura et al., 2015).
